blogs.title: The 'Infinite Investigation': Testing the Temporal Limits of FOIA Exemption 7(A)
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's treatment of the 'pending or reasonably anticipated' requirement under Exemption 7(A). It explores the tension between the passage of time and the continuity of long-term counterterrorism investigations, focusing on how the court used the 'breadth' of the investigation to justify a perpetual status of 'ongoing' proceedings. The post will discuss the implications of this reasoning for FOIA plaintiffs who seek to challenge 'stale' records that may have lost their law enforcement relevance over years of litigation.

blogs.title: Information, Not Words: The High Bar for Segregability in National Security Files
blogs.description: Focusing on the court's analysis of 'reasonably segregable' information, this post examines the distinction between 'meaningful information' and 'individual words.' It explores the 'inextricably intertwined' doctrine and how it allows agencies to withhold massive volumes of records when sensitive data is interspersed throughout the text. The post will argue that this standard creates a significant hurdle for plaintiffs, effectively allowing for 'all-or-nothing' withholdings in complex investigative files.

blogs.title: The Secrecy Paradox: Ex Parte Declarations and the Erosion of FOIA Transparency
blogs.description: This post critiques the court's reliance on ex parte declarations to determine what information is not segregable. It examines the inherent procedural irony of using secret evidence to justify the non-disclosure of public records. By analyzing the court's assertion that such a handicap is 'inherent' to sensitive cases, the post will discuss the broader implications for judicial oversight and the potential for agencies to shield records from meaningful scrutiny behind a veil of sealed evidence.
